- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment history — if sentiment is neutral or negative, model may be overconfident; adjust downward.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of downward trend after peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and model is forecasting upward, model is likely overoptimistic; reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply a 0.5–1% downward adjustment for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model may ignore sentiment — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
